entries.line: Quotes use explicitly sent output counts/duration, text characters, `image_size` dimensions and measured `context.media[audio_url].durationSec`. Missing measurements stay unknown; schema defaults do not supply a duration. Text/JSON results use the queue executor and publish an immutable manifest in `pipeline/model-results/`. Their `--output` may be any file path under the project: it pins operation identity rather than the manifest destination. Training and Kling voice retain their dedicated nonmedia workflow.

entries.line: Tracked exact endpoint tariffs support the four Kling V3 Turbo creation endpoints, O3 pro video reference and create-voice. Generated-second quotes require the explicitly sent output duration; absent, nullable or automatic duration stays unknown even when a public schema describes a default. A helper cannot price five seconds and submit fifteen, or borrow another model's price. Nonmedia voice/training helpers bind the exact registered endpoint, model and result kind to one physical operation; batching requires separate operation identities. Unknown training prices still need an authorised manual bound. Historical resumes reuse their original validated quote and liability, including retired endpoints, without refreshing the price.

entries.line: For supported fixed-duration Seedance creation/reference requests, use the optional versioned `context.videoForecast` procedure below. First dry-run without the forecast and pin the returned endpoint/schema hash and `metadata.inputHash` after imported references resolve. Record output pixels as explicit sourced planning assumptions and every passed video reference in order with its original-string hash and duration evidence; dry-run again to validate. Do not infer output dimensions from aspect ratio, resolution labels or reference frames. Auto/editing/draft/completion and unresolved tariffs remain unknown. Remote URL hashes pin strings, not remote bytes. Frozen evidence belongs to one operation; changed forecasts require a deliberate new generation revision.

entries.line: Use `pnpm models:pick --use-case replace-person`, `--use-case influencer-photo` or `--use-case ad-variant` for Genjutsu character swaps, Soul / AI Influencer personas and Marketing Studio ad stills across providers. Compare labelled exact/tiered prices, floors, release dates and reasons; `pnpm models:compare` reports only evidenced equivalent savings. Scaffold with `pnpm fal:scaffold --provider higgsfield --endpoint ENDPOINT --out REQUEST.json`, retain `provider: "higgsfield"`, then `pnpm hf:quote --request REQUEST.json` and the usual `generate:model --dry-run` loop. Never reuse a fal payload for an identical Higgsfield ID. A schema-less candidate such as Genjutsu Light needs explicit `/estimate` validation (`hf:quote --provider-estimate`) or a schema; catalogue floors never admit a budget. Real people/third-party clips need `entity:card` consent and source-use permissions before provider processing.
